Subject: RAG evaluation — recommended models & next steps

Hi Petr / Katerina,

Thanks again for the call today — good context on the search-first knowledge base use case and the content mix (≈1M docs, ~70% internal engineering/wiki pages, ~30% product/support artifacts). Quick recap and a proposed next step list so we can kick off a focused RAG evaluation pilot.

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Improve grounding (reduce hallucinations) for customer-facing answers and shorten median answer latency to <500ms p50 for simple queries.
- Constraints: On-prem indexing for some docs (security), public cloud for embeddings ok; cost sensitivity in pilot — prefer hosted with measurable unit costs.

Recommended immediate plan (pilot eval)
1) Indexing/retrieval: Hybrid approach — BM25 lexical first pass + dense vector recall for semantic matches. Suggested first-pass config: BM25 (Elasticsearch) with min_should_match tuned, then vector recall with FAISS IVFFlat (sharded) using rw-embed-large-v2 (256-d).
2) Chunking and storage: 500-token fixed chunking with document-level metadata (source, last_updated, confidentiality flag). Deduplicate at ingest by simhash threshold 0.92.
3) Reranker: Cross-encoder reranker for top_k=10 (recommended model: crossenc-rw-base-v1) to improve precision@1 and reduce false positives. For very latency-sensitive flows we can also test a distilled bi-encoder reranker for top_k=3.
4) Generation model(s): For your public/low-sensitivity answers — rw-gen-large-3b-q4a (good cost/quality balance). For customer-sensitive, longer answers (and when higher factuality required) — rw-gen-13b-fp16 (can be pinned to dedicated capacity).
5) Eval metrics and thresholds: grounding_rate (percent of responses with verifiable doc citations) target >92% for pilot; hallucination_rate <6% (sample-based); precision@1 and MRR on manual eval set; top-50 recall for retrieval. Also track end-to-end p50/p95 latency and token cost.

Artifacts attached: ostrava_promptsets_v1.csv (sample prompts + expected behavior), ostrava_rag_eval_template.md (eval plan + metrics). I've also added a folder in Drive with the benchmark skeleton.

Next steps and asks
- Dev: can you confirm whether the 1M docs include scanned PDFs (OCR?) and whether any data must stay on-prem for regulatory reasons?
- Ostrava: please confirm a 2-week window for a 1,000-query pilot set (we'll provide seed prompts).
- Redwood: we will provide an estimated cost range and a proposed pilot SOW.

Proposed timeline
- July 20: pilot seed prompts agreed
- July 27–Aug 3: pilot run + automated metrics
- Aug 5: review results + recommendation (reranker choice + model pinning)

Happy to jump back on a short 30-min call — I can demo the proposed retrieval + reranker behavior with a small sample.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Petr — adding some technical detail to address your questions.

1) Latency: the p50/p95 numbers I shared are end-to-end estimates for a configuration with: BM25 first pass (Elasticsearch, sub-50ms), vector recall (FAISS IVFFlat, sharded, ~60-120ms depending on shard count), cross-encoder rerank (top_k=10, optimized on GPU, ~70-200ms). So for the full stack p50 ~300-450ms is realistic; p95 will depend heavily on load and autoscaling. We can trade latency for cost by lowering rerank_top_k to 3 or using a distilled cross-encoder.

2) Reranker cost/accuracy tradeoff: empirical guidance from similar pilots — full cross-encoder on top-10 typically yields +6-12% precision@1 over bi-encoder-only. Distilled cross-encoder reduces compute by ~60% with ~3-5% lift vs bi-encoder (so still meaningful). Recommendation: pilot with full cross-encoder on top-10 for evaluation only, then test a distilled variant in production to control costs.

3) Hybrid retrieval & scanned PDFs: For OCR-noisy PDFs we'll add an OCR confidence score to metadata and prefer high-confidence sections for citation. For on-prem docs (200k) we suggest a hybrid deployment: keep embeddings on-prem for those docs and route retrieval there; use federation so that ranking and generation can still occur in hosted or dedicated capacity depending on your security needs.

4) Proposed eval config (pilot):
- seed set: 1,000 queries (mix: 40% lookup, 40% multi-doc synthesis, 20% long-form)
- first_pass: BM25 + vector (top_k=50)
- rerank_top_k: 10 (cross-encoder)
- chunk_size: 500 tokens, overlap 50 tokens
- metrics: grounding_rate, hallucination_rate (human-labeled on 250 samples), MRR@10, precision@1, recall@50, end-to-end latency p50/p95, cost per 1k queries

5) Operational notes: sharding vector index by document namespace and time-window will keep query latency stable as we scale. We can provide a set of automation scripts to run the pilot and push metrics to the Redwood Console + your monitoring stack.

I can run a dry demo of the pipeline on a 10k doc sample this week if that helps — Neha, can we lock a 30-min slot?

-Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
